{{short description|Conjecture on the coefficients of cyclotomic polynomials}}
In mathematics, the '''Sister Beiter conjecture''' is a conjecture about the size of coefficients of ternary [[cyclotomic polynomial]]s (i.e. where the index is the product of three prime numbers). It is named after [[Marion Beiter]], a Catholic nun who first proposed it in 1968.{{r|paper68}} 

==Background==
For <math>n\in\mathbb{N}_{>0}</math> the maximal coefficient (in absolute value) of the cyclotomic polynomial <math>\Phi_n(x)</math> is denoted by <math>A(n)</math>.

Let <math>3\leq p\leq q\leq r</math> be three prime numbers. In this case the cyclotomic polynomial <math>\Phi_{pqr}(x)</math> is called ''ternary''. In 1895, A. S. Bang{{r|bang}} proved that <math>A(pqr)\leq p-1</math>. This implies the existence of <math>M(p):=\max\limits_{p\leq q\leq r\text{ prime}}A(pqr)</math> such that <math>1\leq M(p)\leq p-1</math>.

==Statement==
Sister Beiter conjectured{{r|paper68}} in 1968 that <math>M(p)\leq \frac{p+1}{2}</math>. This was later disproved, but a ''corrected Sister Beiter conjecture'' was put forward as <math>M(p)\leq \frac{2}{3}p</math>.

==Status==
A preprint{{r|arxiv23}} from 2023 explains the history in detail and claims to prove this corrected conjecture. Explicitly it claims to prove
<math display=block>
M(p)\leq\frac{2}{3}p  \text{ and } 
\lim\limits_{p\rightarrow\infty}\frac{M(p)}{p}= \frac{2}{3}.
</math>
